# Preface {.unnumbered}

This book is a graduate introduction to affine Toda field theory that leads into current research. It is written for a mathematical physicist who knows quantum field theory but has not met affine Toda theory, Kac–Moody algebras or quantum groups.

**Prerequisites.** Quantum field theory at the level of a first graduate course (path integrals, perturbation theory, renormalization, the S-matrix), finite-dimensional Lie algebras at the level of $su(n)$, and complex analysis. Everything else is developed in the text.

**Structure.** Parts I–IV are textbook material: the physical and algebraic background, the classical theory, and the real-coupling quantum theory. Parts V–VII present research results, many of them new: the semiclassics of complex solitons, exact soliton S-matrices, and the foundations of the imaginary-coupling theories as non-unitary quantum field theories. The [introduction](part1-background/01-introduction.qmd) gives a chapter-by-chapter map.

**Reading paths.**

- *Physics first:* Parts I, III, IV and VI.
- *Mathematics first:* Part II, then Part VII.
- *For specialists:* Parts V–VII, consulting earlier chapters as needed.

**Status.** Chapters marked "To be written" are planned but not yet drafted. Parts V–VII are complete drafts.

Supporting code: [foundations_code](https://github.com/gustavdelius/affine_toda/tree/main/foundations_code) and [soliton_rmatrix_code](https://github.com/gustavdelius/affine_toda/tree/main/soliton_rmatrix_code).
